questions.stem: In a Vernier calipers, when both jaws touch each other, zero of the Vernier scale is shifted to the right of zero of the main scale and $7^{\text{th}}$ Vernier division coincides with a main scale reading. If the value of 1 main scale division is 1 mm and there are 10 Vernier scale divisions, then the Vernier caliper has :
questions.solution:
$L \cdot C \cdot = \frac{1 M \cdot S \cdot D}{n} = 0.1\ \mathrm{mm}$
Zero error is positive as vernier zero lies to right of zero of main scale.
+ve zero error $= V \cdot C \cdot \times L \cdot C \cdot$
$= 7 \times 0.1\ \mathrm{mm}$
$= 0.7\ \mathrm{mm}$
$= 0.07\ \mathrm{cm}$

questions.stem: L, C and R represents physical quantities inductance, capacitance and resistance respectively. The dimensional formula $ML^{2}T^{-4}A^{-2}$ corresponds to _______.
questions.solution:
Lets explore options in a smart way
Quality factor $= \frac{1}{R}\sqrt{\frac{L}{C}}$ = dimensionless
Hence Option D is wrong
Since we know
$\frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} = \omega = T^{-1}$
Now lets explore option A
$R = \frac{V}{I} = \frac{ML^{2}T^{-2}}{I^{2}T} = ML^{2}T^{-3}A^{-2}$
Option A $\frac{R}{\sqrt{LC}} \Rightarrow ML^{2}T^{-3}A^{-2}T^{-1}$
$ML^{2}T^{-4}A^{-2}$ Option A is correct.

questions.stem:
When one moves from a point 16 km below the earth's surface to a point 16 km above the earth's surface. The change in g is approximately $\alpha$ %. The value of $\alpha$ is ______.
(Take radius of the earth = 6400 km.)
questions.solution:
For outside point $g' = \frac{GM}{r^{2}}$
$\frac{\Delta g}{g}\% = -2\frac{\Delta r\%}{r}$
$= -2 \times \frac{16}{6400} \times 100$
$= -0.5\%$
For inside point
$g' = \frac{GMr}{R^{3}}$
$\frac{\Delta g}{g}\% = \frac{\Delta r}{r}\% = -\frac{16}{6400} \times 100 = -0.25\%$
So difference in g between outside point & inside point will be 0.25%.

questions.stem: Three masses $m_{1} = 4$ kg, $m_{2} = 4$ kg and $m_{3} = 6$ kg are suspended from a fixed smooth frictionless pully as shown in the figure below. The value of $T_{1}/T_{2}$ is ______. (take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^{2}}$)

A wedge Y with mass of 10 kg and all frictionless surfaces and the inclined surface making $37^\circ$ with horizontal. A block X with mass 2 kg is placed at the highest point of the wedge as shown in figure is at rest. At $t = 0$ wedge (Y) is pulled toward right with constant force (f) of 24 N. Taking the block X at rest at $t = 0$, the time taken by it to slide down 8.8 m on the slope, while Y is on the move, is ____ s.
(take $\tan 37^\circ = 3/4$ and $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^{2}}$)
questions.solution:
$a_{r}$ = acceleration of 2 kg relative to wedge
FBD of block in wedge frame
[FBD: pseudo force $ma$ horizontally to the left, $mg\sin 37^\circ$ down the incline]
$mg\sin 37 - ma\cos 37^\circ = ma_{r}$
$\frac{5}{4}\left(g\sin 37 - a_{r}\right) = a$ ....(i)
In horizontal direction (on system)
$F_{n} = m_{system}a_{H}$
$24 = 10a + 2a + 2a_{r}\cos 37^\circ$
$24 = 12a + 2a_{r}\cos 37$ .....(ii)
Put a in eq. (ii)
$24 = (12)\left[\left(\frac{5}{4}\left(g \times \frac{3}{5} - a_{r}\right)\right)\right] + 2a_{r}\frac{4}{5}$
$24 = 15 \times \frac{3g}{5} - 15a_{r} + \frac{8a_{r}}{5}$
$\frac{67a_{r}}{5} = 90 - 24$
$a_{r} = \frac{66 \times 5}{67}$
$S = \frac{1}{2}a_{r}t^{2}$
$8.8 = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{66 \times 5}{67}t^{2}$
$0.8 = \frac{30}{2 \times 67}t^{2}$
$t^{2} = \frac{8 \times 2 \times 67}{300} = 3.57 \Rightarrow t \approx 2\ \mathrm{sec}$.

questions.stem:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R:
Statement I : Change in internal energy of a system containing n mole of ideal gas can be written as $\Delta U = nC_{v}\left(T_{f} - T_{i}\right) = \frac{nR}{\gamma - 1}\left(T_{f} - T_{i}\right)$, where $\gamma = \frac{C_{p}}{C_{v}}$, $T_{i}$ = initial temperature, $T_{f}$ = final temperature.
Statement II : Relation between degree of freedom f and $\gamma$ (= $C_{p}/C_{v}$) is $\left(\gamma = 1 + \frac{2}{f}\right)$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explantion of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements :
A. Zeroth law of thermodynamics gives concept of temperature
B. First law of thermodynamics gives concept of internal energy
C. In isothermal expansion of ideal gas, $\Delta Q \neq \Delta W$
D. Product of intensive and extensive variables is extensive
E. The ratio of any extensive variable to mass will be an extensive variable
Choose the correct combination of statements from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Intensive variable : If you divide a system $\rightarrow$ these variable remains same.
Ex. Refractive index of full slab of glass is same as that of half slab.
Extensive variable : If you divide system $\rightarrow$ These variable gets divided.
Ex. Mass
Option A $\rightarrow$ true
Option B $\rightarrow$ true
Option C $\rightarrow$ false, $\Delta Q = W$ as $\Delta U = 0$ for isothermal process.
Option D $\rightarrow$ true
Option E $\rightarrow$ false, for example $1/\rho = V/m$, V is extensive variable but $\rho$ is intensive variable.

questions.stem:
An electron of mass m is moving in an electric field $\vec{E} = -2E_{0}\hat{i}$ ($E_{0}$ = constant > 0), with an initial velocity $\vec{V} = v_{0}\hat{i}$ ($v_{0}$ = constant > 0). If $\lambda_{0} = \frac{h}{4mv_{0}}$, its de Broglie wavelength at time t is _______.
(e = charge of electron)

In the hydrogen atom, the electron makes a transition from the higher orbit (i) to a lower orbit (f). The ratio of the radius of the orbits in given by $r_{i} : r_{f} = 16 : 4$. The wavelength of photon emitted due to this transition is _______ nm. (Given Rydberg constant = $1.0973 \times 10^{7}$/m)
questions.solution:
$r \propto n^{2}$ since ratio is given as 16:4 we are assuming
$n_{i} = 4$
$n_{f} = 2$
$\frac{1}{\lambda} = Rz^{2}\left(\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}} - \frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}\right)$
$\frac{1}{\lambda} = 1.0973 \times 10^{7}\left(\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{16}\right)$
$\frac{1}{\lambda} = 1.0973 \times 10^{7}\frac{3}{16}$
$\lambda = \frac{16}{3} \times \frac{10^{-7}}{1.0973}$
$\lambda = 486\ \mathrm{nm}$

questions.stem: A displacement current of 4.0 A can be set up in the space between two parallel plates of $6\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ capacitor. The rate of change of potential difference across the plates of the capacitor is nearly $\alpha \times 10^{6}$ V/s. The value of $\alpha$ is _________.
Refer to the figure given below, current between terminals A and B is ________A.
questions.solution:
Emf of each branch $= 5 \times 3$
$= 15\ \mathrm{V}$
resistance of each $= 3 \times 3 = 9\ \Omega$
$r_{equivalent} = \frac{9}{3} = 3\ \Omega$
$\varepsilon_{equivalent} = \left(\frac{15}{9} + \frac{15}{9} + \frac{15}{9}\right) \times 3 = 15$
[Equivalent circuit: $E_{eq}$ in series with $r_{eq}$, connected across the $9\ \Omega$ branch between A and B]
$i = \frac{15}{9 + 3} = \frac{5}{4}$ A

A compound microscope is designed with two symmetric biconvex lenses. The objective lens is cut vertically, creating two identical plano-convex lenses. One of them is used in place of original objective lens. To retain same magnification keeping the object distance unchanged, the tube length has to be :
questions.solution:
$MP = \frac{LD}{f_{0}f_{e}}$
As $f_{0}$ becomes twice, length of tube should be doubled to keep M.P. same.

questions.stem: Two wires as shown in the figure below, made of steel and have breaking stress of $12 \times 10^{8}\ \mathrm{N/m^{2}}$. Area of cross-section of upper wire is $0.008\ \mathrm{cm^{2}}$ and of lower wire is $0.004\ \mathrm{cm^{2}}$. The maximum mass that can be added to pan without breaking any wire is _______ kg. (take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^{2}}$)
questions.solution:
Lower wire
$T_{max}$ = Stress $\times$ Area
$T_{max} = 12 \times 10^{8} \times 4 \times 10^{-7}$
$T_{max} = 480$ N
Upper wire
$T_{max} = 12 \times 10^{8} \times 8 \times 10^{-7}$
$T_{max} = 960$ N
For lower wire to break
$480 = mg + 10g$
$m = 38$ kg
For upper wire to break
$960 = mg + (10 + 30)g$
$m = 56g$
max mass should be less than 38 kg for both wire to not break.

A transverse wave on a string is described by $y = 3\sin(36t + 0.018x + \pi/4)$. where x, y are in cm and t in seconds. The least distance between the two successive crests in the wave is _____ cm. (Nearest integer) ($\pi = 3.14$)

In the given circuit below inductance values of $L_{1}$, $L_{2}$ and $L_{3}$ are same. The magnetic energy stored in the entire circuit is ($U_{t}$) and that stored in the $L_{2}$ inductor is ($U_{l}$). $U_{t}/U_{l}$ is ______. (Ignore the mutual inductance if any)
questions.solution:
Current in $L_{2}$ and $L_{3}$ should be same by symmetry
$U_{L} = \frac{1}{2}Li^{2}$
$U_{t} = \frac{1}{2}Li^{2} + \frac{1}{2}Li^{2} + \frac{1}{2}L(2i)^{2}$
$= 3Li^{2}$
$\frac{U_{t}}{U_{L}} = \frac{3Li^{2}}{\frac{1}{2}Li^{2}} = 6$
